outcomes: A provider written against the contracts passes the shared scenarios, and the CLI offers it without a change of its own.
A caller tells a refused, missing, conflicting and uncertain write apart, and knows which read settles an uncertain one.
No binding or envelope carries a credential.
nonGoals: Provider discovery, routing, the RPC bridge and the CLI commands, which cli/collaboration-providers owns.
How a provider maps the contracts onto its backend.
Retrying a provider call on a caller's behalf.
A TypeScript reader of the contracts.

text: Contracts speak v1; missions also v2. tasks requires find, get, create, update and transition and offers assign, claim and link;
proposals requires find, review, status and upsert and offers automerge, comments, merge and screenshots;
memory requires checkpoint, context and mission and offers search;
missions requires ask, reply and sync and offers status. tasks.create, proposals.review, memory.checkpoint and missions.ask take an idempotencyKey.
Only missions.sync is host-only, and only a mutation can be.
The catalog is sorted by contract and version, and each version lists its operations sorted and once, never capabilities.
Each operation has a summary, read or mutating access and its documents; a read is never destructive, takes no precondition, and alone takes the selection.
A request for an unknown contract, unsupported version or unknown operation is refused as unknown_contract, unsupported_version or unknown_operation.

Trailing data, a non-object, invalid JSON or a wrong member type is parse_error, a repeated member duplicate_member and an unknown one unknown_field, at any depth, and a document above 4 MiB too_large.
A bad timestamp is invalid_timestamp, a list or title above its bound too_large, a multi-line title invalid_value; an unknown document type has no validator.
fixtures/expectations.json lists every valid fixture and the exact distinct codes of every invalid one.
Each valid bindings, envelope, response, request and result fixture parses without error;
each invalid one produces exactly its listed codes, all from the closed code list;
a valid request or result re-encodes to a document that parses and encodes to the same bytes.
Every code except parse_error, too_large, invalid_timestamp and invalid_declaration is produced by at least one invalid fixture.

The JSON schemas list, for each operation's input and result and for each shared entity and envelope document, exactly the members the Go types encode, and the bindings object names exactly the contracts.
Each closed vocabulary's enum equals its Go list, which is sorted.
The input schema of every operation, capabilities included, is a closed object with every reference inlined, and an unknown operation has none.
An envelope names a known contract and an operation, and an ok one its version unless it answers capabilities.
An outcome other than ok carries an error and no result. current appears only on conflict and reconcile only on unresolved, where it names an operation of the same contract;
ReconcileOperation returns the first catalog operation a hint names.
A negative version, a nameless provider, and a capabilities result missing what its status needs or naming an unknown access or precondition rule are refused.

A bindings block binds each contract to one provider and one version on its own: an unbound contract stays unbound, and an invalid contract binding is reported under its contract's field and drops only itself.

A block that is not a JSON object, repeats a member, pads a provider name, has no version, requires a required or repeated operation, has settings that are not an object, or exceeds its own or its settings' size bound is refused.

A binding whose settings carry a credential-named member at any depth, or a URL value with a password or with any http or https user, whatever the scheme's case, is refused as credential_setting at that setting's path;
an SSH account, a scp-like remote, an anonymous URL and a path are accepted. apiToken, API_KEY, api-key, Password and Authorization are credential names, repository and remote are not.
The CLI reports such a binding invalid without echoing it.

A provider offers a contract version only when its providers section declares each required operation once, with its precondition rule, atomic for claim, workspaceSelection where the operation takes the selection, and only members the catalog lists for the operation.
Any error withdraws that version; a provider of an unknown version draws one warning.
The local, GitHub, GitLab, Linear and memory providers' manifests draw no diagnostic, and the CLI answers a call to a withdrawn version unsupported.
Serve runs a handler only for a request whose provider call the contract accepts, with its settings and operation key;
any other request is invalid and an operation without a handler unsupported.
A handler that panics, returns an invalid or unencodable result, or fails with outcome ok makes a mutation unresolved, not retryable, and a read unavailable.
A failure keeps its outcome, reason and message, unresolved is never retryable, a nil page is items [], and an undecodable request writes nothing.
page.size is 0 to 100 in schema and validator, and cursor and next share one length bound.
The maximal results of tasks.get and find, proposals.find, status and comments, memory.mission, context and checkpoint, and the maximal checkpoint request, fit the 4 MiB document bound.

Serve shortens a page that would exceed it, so a traversal lists each item once with at most two handler calls a page, and answers unavailable with provider.invalid_response, after one repeat, for a handler that ignores the page size.
The CLI answers a list with no match as items [], and its pages, followed by next, end at the last one.
A page above the requested size is unavailable.
A list page above the 4 MiB document bound is unavailable with provider.invalid_response, not retryable, and its message asks for a page.size below the one requested;
an oversized answer that is no list page, or holds a member above its own bound, gets no such advice.
Every list request of the catalog carries the page the advice names.

requirements.text: A proposal result without labels or assignees keeps them absent, and one with an empty or filled list keeps that list, through a parse and a re-encoding: absent means not reported, [] means none.

text: A proposal may carry pageUrl, a display link to its change in the provider's own console, never an identity, validated like url.
It is a declared member of find, status, upsert, merge and automerge (ADR 0011), declared on every one of them a provider offers or on none, or its proposals version is withdrawn;
a provider that declares it answers it on every proposal, as providertest.RunProposals checks.
Every tasks provider passes providertest.RunTasks, which reports what it creates to Track: a label nobody carries finds items [] without next;
create, get and a repeat with the same idempotencyKey give one task, and that key with other content is a conflict, idempotency.mismatch, not retryable;
pages list a label's tasks once, in one order, also when the size changes;
state, label and text filters match, every label required;
a stale expectedRevision is a conflict;
another source's reference is not_found.
Every proposals provider passes providertest.RunProposals, which reports what it creates to Track: a head with no proposal finds items [];
upsert opens one proposal per exact base and head, a repeat updates it under a new revision, and a stale expectedRevision is a conflict;
each head has its own proposal;
a review repeats by its idempotencyKey, other content under it is idempotency.mismatch, and status lists it once;
labels and assignees agree between answers;
another source's reference is not_found.
proposals.comments, an optional read, lists in bounded pages what people wrote on one proposal.
A comment is ref and body, plus, when known, url, author, submittedAt, the review it belongs to, and the path, line and commit of the file line it is anchored to;
a comment on no file line has no path.
A provider that offers it passes providertest.RunProposals's comment scenario: the body of a published review is listed once across pages, naming that review.

proposals.screenshots, an optional mutation, hands the provider one screenshots manifest: the request is the proposal's ref, the commit captured and the path of the manifest file, at most 4096 bytes on one line.
The result names the proposal, the commit, the project, the captures listed and the files uploaded.
The CLI answers unresolved, with provider.identity_mismatch and the repeat as reconciliation, an ok answer for another proposal or commit.

tasks.get may answer parentProgress (the parent's key, title, link, done and total children), blockedBy and blocking (linked tasks: reference, state, and key, title and link when known) and comments (a count, the last author and time, a link; no body).
Absent means not reported; [] or a zero count means none.
Refused: parentProgress without parent, total under 1 or below done; a linked task without reference or state, or naming the task itself; a negative count; a last comment on a zero count.

A provider names the context members it fills under members of its get operation; the catalog lists what each operation may declare, another member withdraws the contract version, and capabilities reports the declared ones.
The members are outside the task's revision, and only get answers them: the CLI refuses one in any other operation's result.
providertest checks that get returns each declared member and no other, and that the other operations it calls return none.
Every memory provider passes providertest.RunMemory: an unknown mission has no record;
a mustNotExist checkpoint is created, repeated by its key, refused as idempotency.mismatch with other content and as record.exists a second time;
a stale revision is revision.conflict with current;
another instance resumes and repeats;
of 6 concurrent checkpoints or creations exactly one lands;
pages list records once at any size;
a record stays in its workspace;
the largest checkpoint reads back unchanged.
A missions provider keeps one decision per idempotency key: the same content, whatever the mission title, replays it with its answer, and other content is a conflict (idempotency.mismatch).
A message takes one reply; another is a conflict (message.closed).
A delivered answer acknowledges its decision, a delivered message leaves the inbox, unknown or repeated ids change nothing, and an older sync never overwrites a newer one.
Concurrent callers on one store lose no write.

requirements.text: A missions provider keeps, for each session, the stage and the usage of the last applied sync that carried them: a sync without them keeps the stored ones, and an ended session stays ended until a later sync.

text: missions.status, an optional read an agent may call, answers the named mission's view and a page of its sessions, newest observation first, then by engine and id, each once: session, state, observedAt and, when held, stage, usage, branch, error and waitUntil of its last applied sync.
A traversal lists once each session that does not sync during it.
A provider without it is unsupported with operation.unsupported; an answer for another mission is provider.identity_mismatch.

When an applied missions.sync names another mission than the session's last applied sync, the session leaves that mission, and a missions provider retires it once nothing else holds it: no other session's last applied sync names it, and it holds no decision and no message; a provider that also serves memory keeps a mission whose memory holds a record.
A retired mission reads as one the provider does not hold: its key, an empty title, an empty plan, no open decision and no session.
missions.sync and missions.status declare missedSyncs, a request member of version 1: count, reason and lastAt.
The CLI removes it from a request to a provider that does not declare it.
A provider that declares it keeps each session's missedSyncs of the last applied sync that carried one, and status answers it.
providertest checks that a declaring provider answers the one it kept.

requirements.text: The scenarios normalize each request before it reaches Serve: a list request without a page gets page.size 20 and an explicit size is kept, a memory request without a workspace gets the served one and one naming its own keeps it, and a request the contract refuses is sent unchanged.

text: The CLI refuses a call before it starts the provider: an optional operation the provider does not offer is unsupported with operation.unsupported, an operation the contract lacks or a request it refuses is invalid with request.invalid, and expectedRevision or mustNotExist sent to a provider whose operation declares preconditions none is unsupported with precondition.unsupported, never dropped.
It recognizes every precondition member of the catalog, and no operation that takes none carries one.
The CLI answers unavailable with provider.identity_mismatch a read for another task, proposal, head or mission, or with a state or kind outside its filter;

and unresolved, not retryable, with a reconcile, a mutation that does: an update or upsert for another item, head or head commit, a transition to another state, a claim for another holder or still held after release, a review of another commit, a merge that did not merge, an automerge answering a closed proposal, or a checkpoint that kept its revision.
An ok missions.sync answer describes the mission key the sync named, whatever the sync's age, reports only the decisions it named and answers each reply it carried once;
an ok missions.reply answer names the message;
a new missions.ask answer is an open decision.
Any other answer is unresolved with reason provider.identity_mismatch, and an unresolved missions write names its own repeat as the reconciliation.
A provider that cannot start is unavailable, not retryable.
A read that times out or is canceled, or a call stopped before its provider starts, is unavailable and retryable.
A mutation whose provider started, then timed out, was canceled, failed or wrote no valid answer is unresolved, not retryable, and its reconcile names a read or the keyed repeat;
a read whose provider failed or wrote no valid answer is unavailable, not retryable.

The CLI refuses a provider answer the contract refuses, with provider.invalid_response: an answer that is not one response document (a second document, trailing data), or a read answering conflict or unresolved, makes the read unavailable;
an invalid result makes a mutation unresolved.
A provider that answers a failure keeps its outcome.
The CLI keeps provider standard error out of every envelope.

It removes from every message and result each credential-named environment value the provider inherits and any URL userinfo, matching the decoded value whatever its JSON spelling, keeping member order, and leaving a result without the secret unchanged.
A result it cannot redact in place is withheld: unavailable for a read, unresolved for a write.

requirements.text: A caller does not repeat a write answered unresolved: putnami change finalize sends a proposal upsert answered unresolved once, then stops with an error before any dependent write, such as a task transition.

text: Every version 1 document frozen in fixtures/v1 on 2026-11-07, at least one per contract and document kind, parses without error under the current module, and its bytes match the SHA-256 the test pins.
A change that would reject or rewrite one opens a new contract version.
missions version 2 holds every version 1 operation with the same request and result documents, and also requires report, runs and start; missions.start takes an idempotencyKey.
A provider that declares missions version 2 is also offered version 1, restricted to the version 1 operations it declares, and the CLI calls it with the version the workspace bound.
A run carries id, mission, kind, state, input, startedAt and, once ended, endedAt; result when succeeded, failure when failed; session optional.
Kinds: audit, build, rebase, review, triage. input and result hold one member, named by the kind, each closed.
A finding has severity (high, medium, low, info), title, optional file, line, body; at most 100 per result, texts at most 64 KiB.
A review result has commit, verdict, findings; an audit result scope, revision, verdict (pass, concerns, fail), findings.
missions.start creates a running run; the same idempotencyKey with the same content replays it, and other content is a conflict (idempotency.mismatch).

missions.report ends a running run once: the same report replays, another is a conflict (run.closed), an unknown run is not_found (run.not_found), and a result of another kind is invalid (run.kind_mismatch).
missions.runs pages a mission's runs, optionally of one kind, latest start first (at one instant, the last started first), each once.
An ok missions.start answer names the requested mission and kind and, unless replayed, a running run;
an ok missions.report answer names the requested run in a final state;
an ok missions.runs page holds only runs of the named mission and kind, no more than the page size.
Any other answer is provider.identity_mismatch: unresolved for a write, unavailable for a read.
@putnami/local-collaboration declares missions version 2, passes the run scenarios, and still passes the missions scenarios on version 1 and version 2.
